authority: Base Demos + Investigations PM owns universal plan-first + rendering mechanics; this profile owns Algebra-specific build scope, type libraries, source routing, graph-tool expectations, timing, representations, paths, CSS, and plan QA.

bank_policy.role_if_supplied: secondary consistency/reference only; may reuse current vocabulary or approved representation bytes when genuinely useful; never convert Bank routes into Investigation question sets by default

demo.purpose: curiosity/intellectual-tension hook and bridge into instruction; not a mini-lecture
demo.carry_forward_rule: When a later slide depends on earlier evidence, explicitly tell students to copy/record it before advancing. Later slides normally use the student-recorded evidence and do not re-display the earlier table/graph/data. Repeat prior evidence only by explicit teacher choice or genuine accessibility/safety need.
demo.final_slide: 2-4 discussion questions with suggested/acceptable responses in the teacher guide, plus a concise bridge into instruction.
demo.flow_rule: The plan chooses the hook choreography section by section. No universal Observe/Record -> Use Notes -> Reveal middle sequence. Preserve only the dependency/student-record rule when later evidence depends on an earlier slide, and the required final discussion.

investigation.usage_mode: print/Notability-friendly student handout with clean screen preview
investigation.purpose: optional discovery/modeling/representation experience that creates learning through substantive student action
investigation.student_visual_rule: clean hierarchy, minimal decorative boxes; cards/borders only when functionally part of the task; prompt before representation; no descriptive captions
investigation.flow_rule: No universal Task 1 / Task 2 structure and no fixed phase count. The plan-assigned Investigation type controls the classroom sequence. Preserve a useful synthesis/debrief, but let movement, data collection, making/building, gallery/sort, graph/model, or other experience types determine the student pages.

teacher_guide.demo_detail: After the overview, one page per slide: slide replica on top half; detailed slide-specific teacher notes below, including expected responses/what to notice.
teacher_guide.investigation_detail: After the overview, mirror substantive student task phases with answer/solution and rationale/what-to-listen-for; open-ended tasks include validity criteria. Keep Strong Synthesis in the overview and also finish with a student-style synthesis replica plus suggested/acceptable responses, rationale, and teacher press questions.
teacher_guide.table_style: compact polished tables; clear header hierarchy; restrained row rules; center numeric data when appropriate

representations.rule: Use applicable forms substantively; Investigations should often ask students to connect/build/compare representations rather than merely view them.

source_route: original Unit Assessment Plan exact learning target/I-cans
GRAPH_TOOL_CAPABILITY_INVENTORY.md + tools/~graph_tool_v12.py when a new supported authoring visual is needed
legacy_policy: Old Demos/Investigations may supply a useful activity idea or teacher-live improvement, but current Framework/Assessment Plan outranks stale content/layout. Do not preserve a legacy title or task merely because it exists.

package.mode: one course-root drop-in ZIP for all requested Units

demo_mode_library.best_for: a visible structure, surprising result, or concrete model that can launch a mathematical question
prediction from partial information, then reveal/compare an authoritative graph or data display
surfacing competing intuitions before evidence is shown
rate/change, number-line position, graph-as-motion, ordering, or embodied comparison
students choose, defend, and revise among plausible equations/graphs/representations
a fast measurement/count/survey that creates authentic data for the section idea
a tempting wrong claim/model that creates useful tension
students first make/sketch/arrange something, then compare to a mathematical representation
connecting Graph / Equation / Table / Context without turning every section into the same card-sort routine

investigation_mode_library.student_action: match, construct missing views, translate, and defend connections among Graph / Equation / Table / Context
measure/count/time/record data, organize a table, graph/model it, and interpret parameters
physically position/move/order to model a number line, graph, rate, inequality, or comparison, then formalize the mathematics
construct or arrange an area model, algebra-tile model, card system, paper model, or other representation and connect it to symbols
use authoritative graphs/comparison grids as evidence; predict, sort, compare, reverse-engineer, or explain transformations/relationships
analyze class/generated data with scatter plots, bar charts, histograms, or trend/model reasoning
start from a meaningful situation and decide which table/equation/graph/model is defensible rather than being told the representation
evaluate competing student work/models/claims, locate the contradiction, and repair the reasoning
move among posted representations/examples, classify or pair them, then justify patterns and disagreements
create an example/representation satisfying constraints, trade it, and have another group reconstruct or identify missing forms
use an approved graphing/simulation/tool interaction when it creates a learning experience unavailable or clumsy on paper

graph_tool_authoring.rule: Use the authoritative tool whenever a supported graph/model/data display cleanly serves the Demo or Investigation. This is an authoring workflow, so Demos/Investigations are allowed to generate new visuals. Do not use graphs decoratively or when students should construct the graph themselves.
high_value_algebra_capabilities: bar charts, histograms, and scatter plots
fraction/tape models and algebra tiles when useful
graph_tool_authoring.representation_heavy_default: For a representation-heavy target, prefer actual high-quality graph/model output from the tool unless the investigation intentionally asks students to create that representation from scratch.
graph_tool_authoring.plan_gate: Every planned section must make an explicit graph decision before rendering. The decision may be generated evidence/reveal, student construction, or no graph with reason.
graph_tool_authoring.sanity_check: For an all-40-section Algebra plan, zero or near-zero planned tool-generated graph/model uses is a PLAN FAILURE unless the plan clearly shows that students themselves construct those representations in the graph-heavy sections. Re-plan before HTML; do not wait for final output to discover that graphs disappeared.

prototype_guard: U1.1 and any approved prototype define visual quality/teacher-guide structure, not the required task mechanics. Do not clone its card/match/four-view sequence across sections unless that sequence independently fits the section.

plan_first_gate.purpose: Choose the actual classroom experience for all 40 sections before rendering so the builder cannot discover the course one generic worksheet at a time.
investigation_fields_per_section: why this experience fits the section
qa_before_rendering: Every active section has a complete Investigation type and experience sequence.
A type label is not enough: the student action, materials, artifact, and sequence must make that type real.
Scan for repeated sequence signatures caused by template convenience; re-plan suspicious clusters before HTML.
Representation-heavy sections cannot default to text-only without a section-specific reason.
Movement/making/data/gallery/model types must have corresponding real steps/materials/artifacts.
Graph decisions are explicit for every section.
render_fidelity: HTML is downstream of the plan: do not silently change Investigation type during rendering.
Do not reduce movement, data collection, making/building, gallery/sort, graph/model, or create/trade plans to generic Task 1 + Task 2 worksheets.
If graph_decision says tool_generated_student_evidence, an actual generated graph/model/data visual must appear in student-facing assets.
If graph_decision says tool_generated_teacher_reveal, the actual reveal must appear in the Demo/teacher workflow and teacher guide.
If graph_decision says student_constructed_representation, provide appropriate blank graph/data/scaffold and expected solution guidance in the teacher guide.
The final output should be auditable against the packaged plan artifacts.
plan_first_gate.philosophy_alignment: The map is an authoring design hypothesis for optional resources, not a fixed calendar or mandate. Teacher may skip, alter, combine, reorder, or replace resources. Do not create artificial variety quotas; choose experiences by purpose.

workflow_order: PHASE 1: read Philosophy + Framework/Assessment Plans and create complete ~demos_investigations_build_plan.json + .html for all requested sections
PHASE 1 QA: audit the plan for section-fit, real type/action differences, representations, graph decisions, materials, and sequence fidelity
PHASE 2: generate any tool-created figures/data/models required by the plan
PHASE 3: render Demo/Investigation student HTML + teacher guides from the plan; do not silently change types
PHASE 4: audit final output against the plan and package one real ZIP
investigation_type_rule: Choose from the Algebra mode library when it fits. A custom type is allowed when the exact section learning job calls for a different experience; name it clearly and justify it in the plan. The library is a menu, not a quota.
